chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Awn, from one of them, who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying that the newborn does not inherit anything from the wergild until it moves and its voice is heard.
ai.seo_question: When does a newborn baby become eligible to inherit blood money (diyah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic threshold for a fetus's inheritance rights, specifying that mere biological life is insufficient; the infant must exhibit independent signs of life, such as movement and an audible cry, to claim a share of the blood money (diyah). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the state of the womb and the state of a viable newborn, ensuring that inheritance distribution occurs only when the heir is legally recognized as a distinct, living entity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Awn, from one of them who said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying that the new born does not inherit anything from the wergild until it moves and his voice is heard’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ibn ‘Awn from certain persons of them who has narrated the following: “I once heard him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘A newborn does not inherit from a wergild anything unless he cries at the time of birth and his voice is heard.’”
